borders.before: The lecture's welcome, series overview, and learning outcomes.
borders.after: The foundational definition of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease driven by micro-evolution.
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 1 is lecture opening and administrative framing, while subtopic 2 begins the substantive subject matter.
borders.caseForMoving: There is no earlier subtopic, and moving to subtopic 3 would orphan the fundamental definition of cancer in the introductory framing.
borders.caseForRemoving: Removing the border would conflate course housekeeping and pedagogical framing with substantive biology.

borders.before: Global epidemiological patterns, geographic cancer incidence variation, and migrant studies comparing genetics versus environment.
borders.after: A survey of infectious agents and pathogens that drive cancer development.
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 6 concludes the high-level discussion of cancer etiology and epidemiological evidence, while subtopic 7 starts the specific exploration of biological carcinogens (pathogens).
borders.caseForMoving: Moving the border to subtopic 8 would separate the general introduction of pathogens from the detailed Burkitt lymphoma case study.
borders.caseForRemoving: Removing the border would merge general epidemiological framing of cancer risk with the specific biological study of pathogens.

borders.before: The mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma pathogenesis involving EBV, malaria, and Myc translocation.
borders.after: Dietary carcinogens and the biochemical activation of aflatoxin into reactive DNA adducts.
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopics 7–8 deal specifically with infectious pathogens, whereas subtopic 9 shifts to non-biological chemical mutagens and dietary exposures.
borders.caseForMoving: Moving to subtopic 10 would place aflatoxin, a chemical toxin, into the pathogen section.
borders.caseForRemoving: Removing the border would lump together distinct biological infectious agents and chemical/physical carcinogens under one overly broad topic.

borders.before: A summary of the mechanisms of DNA damage, xenobiotic metabolism, tumor promotion, and tissue/developmental stage susceptibility.
borders.after: High-throughput whole-genome sequencing and mutational signatures used to identify carcinogen exposure.
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 17 completes the mechanistic breakdown of carcinogenesis, and subtopic 18 initiates the methodologies used to detect and prove carcinogenicity.
borders.caseForMoving: Moving the border to subtopic 17 would detach the concluding mechanistic summary from the specific mechanisms it summarizes.
borders.caseForRemoving: Removing the border would blend the biological mechanisms of how carcinogens act with the research methods used to detect and prove them.

borders.before: The Ames test and the technical limitations of in vitro mutagenicity testing.
borders.after: The concluding synthesis of environmental risk versus benefit and closing remarks.
borders.caseForKeeping: Subtopic 21 ends the evaluation of scientific testing methodologies, while subtopic 22 provides the closing framing and lecture summary.
borders.caseForMoving: Moving the border earlier to subtopic 21 would mix experimental in vitro testing with the concluding summary.
borders.caseForRemoving: Removing the border would append the lecture conclusion onto the discussion of in vitro laboratory assays.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopics 2–3 discuss the theoretical and endogenous foundations of cancer etiology, whereas subtopics 4–6 address external environmental exposures and population epidemiology.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Subtopics 2–6 together build a single coherent overview of cancer etiology by weighing intrinsic cellular bad luck against environmental factors and epidemiological evidence.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopic 7 lists various infectious pathogens generally, whereas subtopic 8 focuses exclusively on the historical and molecular case study of Burkitt lymphoma.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Subtopic 8 serves as the extended, in-depth mechanistic illustration of the infectious oncogenesis principles established in subtopic 7.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopics 9–13 detail direct chemical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolism, while subtopics 14–17 focus on non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: All subtopics (9–17) form a continuous exploration of molecular mechanisms of carcinogenesis, systematically covering direct mutagens, promoters, and host factors before summarizing them in subtopic 17.

insides.caseForDividing: Subtopic 18 examines molecular mutational signatures in DNA, while subtopics 19–21 review traditional epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro validation assays.
insides.caseForKeepingWhole: Subtopics 18–21 collectively present the complete spectrum of complementary methodologies used by researchers to determine and validate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: Introduces the lecturer, the structure of the cancer lecture series, and the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Risk versus Environmental Factors
topics.groupedBecause: Explores the fundamental drivers of cancer development, comparing intrinsic genetic mutations and endogenous cellular errors with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Causes of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Examines how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms demonstrated by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical Mutagens, Promoters, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: Details how chemical carcinogens and radiation damage DNA through direct adducts, metabolic activation, tumor promotion, and developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Determining and Validating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: Describes the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro experimental strategies used to detect and evaluate carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Assessment
topics.groupedBecause: Summarizes the lecture's core themes regarding environmental cancer risk and balances carcinogenic hazards against practical everyday choices.
